tasks.task: Turn customer notes into a one-page problem brief

items.when: When you have interview notes, tickets or reviews and need one page before anyone designs
When the notes are long, to pull the patterns out before you write the brief
When the problem reads like a feature wish, to find the job and the struggling moment
When nobody can say what the customer used before and why they would switch
Before the brief goes out, to tie every stated fact to a note, ticket or number

tasks.task: Cut an idea to a small first version and size it

items.when: When an idea or a pile of feedback needs a problem brief and a first-version scope
When a founder asks what to build first and you need the steps from idea to spec
When the scope keeps growing, to shape a six-week bet and list what to say no to
When there are two honest ways to cut the scope, to see both with cost and dates
When the client asks how long the first version takes and the team builds with AI agents
Before the scope is agreed, to find the hidden guesses that would sink it

tasks.task: Write a product requirements document for one feature

items.when: When the problem is agreed and the team needs a PRD with goals, scope and open questions
When the PRD needs the user's path drawn, with choices, error states and drop-off points
Before sign-off, to rate value, ease of use, build and business risk for the feature
When the PRD lists features to ship but never says which risk each one tests

tasks.task: Write user stories with acceptance criteria

items.when: When the PRD is agreed and the team needs stories they can build and test from
When there is only a feature idea and you need stories with criteria and a sprint plan
When user stories read like a wish list, to try the when, I want, so I can format
When stories are written, to turn each into test steps and see which cannot be tested

tasks.task: Prioritise a long backlog or request list

items.when: When a long list must become a short plan with each item scored and the scoring shown
Before scoring, to pick the ranking method that suits this backlog and this team
When you need every feature scored for reach, impact, confidence and effort, then ranked
When the question is what fits next sprint given the team's real capacity
When everything scores about the same and the list needs a hard cut to one main job

tasks.task: Build a one-quarter roadmap tied to goals

items.when: Before each quarter, to run planning, the request screen and the monthly update in order
When goals are set and each roadmap item must be written as a bet with a reason
When the quarter has no clear goals yet and the roadmap needs measurable results to aim at
When you have an outcome but no clear route, to map opportunities, ideas and tests
When the roadmap should be results to reach, not a feature list, with an update to send
When the quarter could go two ways, to put both plans on a page with dates and a pick
Before the roadmap is shared, to imagine it failed and name the reasons now

tasks.task: Screen a feature request and reply with a reason

items.when: When a request arrives from a customer, sales or the founder and needs a clear answer
When several requests arrive at once, to rule on each and show the full cost of a yes
When there is no rule to screen against, to set the current bet first
When the answer is no, to write a reply the customer accepts with the real reason

tasks.task: Plan and run customer discovery interviews

items.when: When you have an idea and need your guesses, who to talk to and questions that test them
When the questions invite polite praise, to rewrite them so answers are about real past acts
When you must ask strangers or customers for a call and need the message to send

tasks.task: Test demand for an idea before building it

items.when: Before any test, to find the few guesses the plan stands on and rank the riskiest
When you know the riskiest guess and need the smallest test with a pivot or keep rule
When you want several cheap test types to compare, such as a landing page or pre-order
When the team wants to build more before learning what customers actually do

tasks.task: Plan a prototype and what to fake by hand

items.when: When you need one thing to test, three to five features, a build schedule and pass marks
When a clickable web app made by chat is enough to put in front of five users
Before sessions start, to find test blockers and word the tasks neutrally

tasks.task: Set success and guardrail metrics for a feature

items.when: Before building or launching, to agree how you will know it worked and what must not drop
When the product has no single number to steer by and feature goals do not add up
When the metric cannot be measured yet and engineers need an event list and names
When the metrics count clicks, to check they measure the customer's progress

tasks.task: Design an A/B test or a feature-flag rollout

items.when: When you have a change to test and need a hypothesis, sample size and reading plan
Before you commit to a test, to see if the traffic can prove anything and in how many weeks
When tests are many and small, to choose the one change tied to what users would miss

tasks.task: Read out a finished experiment and make the call

items.when: When a test or rollout has finished and you need a readout that ends in a decision
Before reading the lift, to decide whether the test's numbers can be trusted at all
When you have the raw test data and need a split check, ranges and a ship call
When the owner needs the result of two versions explained in plain words

tasks.task: Plan and check a small release

items.when: When a feature is built and accepted and a launch date is agreed
In the week before release, to find gaps in support, tracking, payments and rollback
When the release needs timing, channels and announcement copy in one plan
When the date is fixed and the scope is not, to see the launch at half the size
When the release needs a staged rollout and a rollback plan written down

tasks.task: Write a roadmap update for stakeholders

items.when: Monthly or at cycle end, to say what was done, what is next, what changed and why
When the same update must be told three ways, for executives, engineers and customers
When the update carries bad news, such as a slipped date or a cut feature
Before sending, to check each number and date in the update against its source
When the update goes to a board or client, to read it as they would and list what they must ask

tasks.task: Write release notes and help content for a release

items.when: When engineers hand you a list of merged changes and you need a clean changelog entry
When the notes must be written for customers, not engineers, in more than one version
When support will get questions on day one and needs a help article and FAQ ready
When the notes are full of internal names, to put them in words customers use

tasks.task: Plan and check an AI feature before it ships

items.when: When a chatbot, summariser or recommender needs rules, failure tests and human review
When you need a test plan with scores and human review to catch weak answers
When the feature uses personal data, to write the assessment with conditions and owners
When the pilot has run, to compare results with the baseline and make a go or stop call

tasks.task: Triage a pile of product feedback

items.when: When feedback sits in tickets, scores and calls, to get one ranked signal of need
When feedback arrives every week and each request needs counting and a ruling
When one theme keeps coming up and deserves its own problem brief

tasks.task: Compare rivals' features, pricing and position

items.when: When you have facts on one rival and need their features and pricing set against yours
When you need a feature grid across several rivals for the team
Before sharing, to give every rival price and feature a dated source or cut it

tasks.task: Write a product strategy and vision

items.when: When the team needs vision, customers, trade-offs and metrics on one canvas
When the product could stand for several things, to compare ways to stand apart
When the strategy is drafted, to find where it is a goal list with no diagnosis

tasks.task: Find where new users drop off and plan the fix

items.when: When you have visit, sign-up and day-30 numbers and need the biggest leak named
When the leak is in the first session, to plan a faster path to first value

tasks.task: Review a live feature and keep, fix or retire it

items.when: When a feature has been live a while and you must decide to keep, improve or retire it
When you have the numbers, to show trends against targets and what moved

tasks.task: Turn meeting notes into minutes and a decision record

items.when: When you have rough notes and need decisions, actions with owners and open questions
When a product choice needs a memo with options, risks, missing facts and a review date

always.when: Before any document leaves, to tie each number and customer claim to a dated source
Before a spec or update is shared, to catch typos and one feature named two ways
When you have made two or more options, to let a fresh reviewer pick one against the brief

helpers.when: When the feature needs flows, wireframes or a usability test, not only a written spec
When the decision rests on usage data, cohorts or a test that needs proper analysis
When the problem needs a real interview or survey study before any scope is set
When scope or estimate depends on how the system is built and what is hard to change
When the launch needs positioning, messaging and sales material beyond a checklist
When the feature changes plans, tiers or what customers pay

gaps: No library item writes a post-launch review that compares a release with its success metrics plan
No library item writes customer-facing release notes from a PRD; the changelog items start from code commits
No library item makes two or three clearly different first-version scopes for one idea to compare side by side
No library item checks a PRD for missing parts such as non-goals, guardrail metrics and open questions
No library item plans dependencies between teams for a roadmap or shows what blocks what
No library item runs a Kano or opportunity-score survey to rank features by customer need
No library item estimates software effort and cost from a written scope for a team that does not use AI agents
